title: Go sales CSV report
context: HTTP handler that exports a CSV sales report from PostgreSQL via database/sql. The `sort` query parameter may only be "date", "region" or "total"; anything else falls back to date order. Amounts are stored as integer cents and must be printed as dollars with two decimals. Database resources must always be released and a failed query must never produce a silently truncated report.
code: query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT sold_on, region, total_cents FROM sales WHERE sold_on >= $1 ORDER BY %s", col)

expected.why: unknown values fall back to the raw query parameter, which is pasted into ORDER BY (SQL injection) instead of defaulting to sold_on
rows is never closed (no defer rows.Close()), so the early return on a Scan error leaks the connection
rows.Err() is never checked after the loop, so an error mid-iteration produces a silently truncated report
integer division happens before the conversion, so the cents are dropped and every total ends in .00
